sections.title: Basic Concept of Partnership
sections.content: When two or more people invest money in a business and share profits or losses, it is called a partnership. Profits are shared in the ratio of capital invested. Example: Ram invests ₹10000 and Shyam invests ₹20000, so profit will be shared in 1:2 ratio.

sections.title: Partnership in ₹
sections.content: If total profit is ₹3000 and the capital ratio is 1:2, total parts = 1 + 2 = 3. Ram's share = (1/3) × 3000 = ₹1000. Shyam's share = (2/3) × 3000 = ₹2000.

sections.title: Effect of Time
sections.content: If partners invest for different durations, profit is shared in the ratio of (Capital × Time). Example: Ajay invests ₹10000 for 12 months and Vijay invests ₹10000 for 6 months. Ratio = 10000×12 : 10000×6 = 12:6 = 2:1.

sections.title: Important Formulas
sections.content:
1. Profit ratio = Capital × Time ratio.
2. Individual Profit = (Person's ratio / Total ratio) × Total Profit.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Considering only capital and ignoring time.
2. Forgetting to add total parts.
3. Dividing profit equally without ratio.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In partnership, profit or loss is shared in Capital × Time ratio. First calculate Capital × Time for each partner, then form the ratio and divide profit accordingly.

tricks.title: Quick Ratio Trick
tricks.explanation: If capitals are equal, just take time ratio.
tricks.example: ₹5000 each, one for 12 months, one for 6 months → ratio 12:6 = 2:1.

tricks.title: Same Time Investment
tricks.explanation: If time is same, use only capital ratio.

tricks.title: Quick Profit Division
tricks.explanation: Add total ratio first, then divide profit into parts.
tricks.example: Ratio 2:3, Profit ₹5000 → total parts 5 → one part ₹1000.

tricks.title: Mental Capital × Time
tricks.explanation: Break big numbers mentally for faster multiplication.

tricks.title: Equal Effect Rule
tricks.explanation: If Capital × Time is equal, profits are equal.

tricks.title: One Part Quick Calculation
tricks.explanation: Divide total profit by total parts to get one part.
tricks.example: Profit ₹9000, ratio 3:2 → total parts 5 → one part ₹1800.

tricks.title: Simplify Ratio Fast
tricks.explanation: Reduce ratio to simplest form quickly.

tricks.title: Loss Sharing Rule
tricks.explanation: Loss is shared in the same ratio as profit.

tricks.title: Double Capital, Double Profit
tricks.explanation: If capital is doubled and time same, profit doubles.
